memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment, PURPS (age 30.5 min, OPERATOR class):

Ticket size: $5 at most, or refuse. The pool is deep enough (701 SOL), but the curve is effectively controlled: bundle share 1.0, top-5 buyers 99.9% of early buys, launch bot present, and sell-to-buy ratio 0.0017 in the first two minutes. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% are small against that concentration risk.

If we buy anyway: stop at -20%, hold no longer than 30 min, exit at the first sign of net selling in the last-15-min window (already negative flow of -1.44 SOL is a warning).

Refuse if the operator-cluster pattern reverses (sell pressure from top wallets), if drawdown from the 30-min high exceeds 20%, or if the desk can't size below $10. My recommendation is to skip: the operator base rate is roughly break-even before our fees, which makes this a negative expected-value trade after costs.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying PURPS now is weak. The brief shows an OPERATOR-class coin: 602 SOL bought in the first two minutes from 15 wallets, a launch bot present, and top-5 buyers holding 99.9% of early flow. That concentration is exactly the setup where one party controls the float. The bundle_share and top3_share of 1.0 point the same way.

The recent flow is the only mildly constructive signal: 43 buyers and 9.95 SOL bought over the last 15 minutes, net positive at 1.44 SOL, with a 30 min return of +6.4% and a drawdown of only 0.07% from the 30-minute high. But 8.51 SOL was sold against 9.95 bought, so most of the recent buying was matched by selling, and the 30-minute high-hold reflects a price that barely moved, not broad demand. Pool depth of 701 SOL is decent, yet a single large holder exiting would overwhelm it.

Operator-backed coins have roughly broken even in base rates, and after 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, break-even is a losing trade. Nothing here says demand will still be present in 30-60 minutes independent of the operator's intentions. My recommendation is to skip. If the desk wants exposure to this name, the place to revisit is after the operator's concentration
memos.skeptic:

In the first two minutes after graduation, 602 SOL came in from only 15 wallets, with the top five buyers taking 99.9% of it. That is a concentrated supply base that can exit at any time.

Recent flow is weak: last 15 minutes show 8.51 SOL sold against 9.95 bought, and 30 sellers against 43 buyers. Net flow of 1.44 SOL on a 701 SOL pool is shallow, so a $20 buy plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost leaves little room. The 0.37% return and 0.07% drawdown mean there is no clean dip to enter. Operator-backed coins have roughly broken even, so the expected edge after fees is negative. Skip.
